prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a two-tiered store shelf directly in front of the camera wearer, retreating slightly from roughly 0.4–0.8 m away in frame 1 to 0.7–1.2 m in frames 2–5 as the viewpoint steps back and pans slightly left, with background walls and windows over 3–5 m behind the shelving unit. On the upper shelf (left to right: Viva paper towels, stacked Kleenex boxes, and Scott toilet paper rolls, spaced 0.1–0.3 m apart) and lower shelf (napkin packs, Dixie paper plates, red plastic cups, and round containers, roughly 0.3–0.4 m below the top tier), all items sit within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and a second person standing immediately to the left. Across frames 3 to 5, this second person's right arm (and partial head/torso at the far left edge in frame 5, facing right toward the shelf rather than looking at the camera wearer) enters the foreground at 0.3–0.6 m from the camera, reaching under the upper shelf overhang to grasp and pull out a pack of Dixie plates in frame 5, which partially occludes the lower-shelf boxes behind it. The depth map makes the continuous 3D receding plane of the shelf ledge, the recess depth beneath the upper shelf overhang, and the exact foreground separation between the reaching arm and the shelf items much clearer than in the RGB strip alone. However, the map is unreliable where it merges adjacent packages (such as the Viva rolls and Kleenex boxes) into smooth, undifferentiated blocks and flattens the distant room ceiling and windows into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map attempts to parse the objects on the two-tiered retail shelf (0.4–1.2 m in front of the camera wearer) and the person entering on the left (0.3–0.6 m away), while leaving most of the background room and shelving unlabelled. In frames 3 and 5, it segments the reaching left-side person's right arm (and in frame 5, a separate mask for their cropped head at the top-left edge, facing right toward the shelves and away from the camera wearer) as 'person' in pink and light blue, showing the arm extending rightward in front of the lower shelf within arm's reach of the plates. While this foreground 'person' mask cleanly isolates the silhouette of the reaching arm against the dark, shadowed space beneath the upper shelf where the dark sleeve blends into the background in RGB, the rest of the segmentation map is highly unreliable and temporally inconsistent. In frames 1 and 2, the entire foreground shelf unit is misclassified as a giant mint-green 'refrigerator' mask (spanning 0.4–1.0 m depth), and the vertical sleeve of red plastic cups on the lower shelf (0.1–0.2 m left of the round containers and 0.3 m below the upper shelf) is repeatedly mislabelled as a 'bottle' across frames 1, 2, 4, and 5. Additionally, two Viva paper towel rolls on the upper left shelf are mislabelled as 'bottle' only in frame 3, while theperson's arm in frame 4, the held Dixie plates in frame 5, and almost all other packages on both tiers are completely missed.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, detecting only a single, compact cluster of yellow body keypoints near the bottom-left of frame 3 where the second person's right hand reaches toward the lower shelf. In the RGB context, this person stands just outside the left frame boundary (roughly 0.3–0.6 m from the camera wearer and 0.2–0.5 m from the shelf items), facing rightward toward the shelves rather than toward the camera wearer, with their right arm extending in front of the lower-left shelf tier to grasp a pack of plates within arm's reach before retracting slightly in frame 5. Because nearly the entire body of this person (except their right arm and a sliver of their head and shoulder in frame 5) is cropped out of view by the left edge of the camera frustum and partially occluded by the upper shelf ledge in frames 3–4, the pose estimator fails to establish a valid human skeleton. The map is severely unreliable here: it completely misses the visible arm, hand, and head in frames 4 and 5, provides no magenta hand keypoints in any frame, and collapses an entire full-body skeleton hallucination onto the small visible wrist/hand region in frame 3. Consequently, it adds no spatial information beyond pinpointing the 2D image location of the reaching hand in frame 3, which is already visible in the RGB image.
